newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money jumps to 4.00/4.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money jumps to 4.00/4.50 pct.

text.p: German call money rates shot higher on Thursday trading up to 4.00/4.50 as banks scrambled to meet month-end requirements, but traders said they expected rates to normalise again this afternoon.
On Thursday overnight funds began trading around 3.50 percent and topped around 4.50 percent compared with Wednesday's 3.00/3.10 percent rates.
"This is all related to month-end and is rather normal," one dealer said, adding that the gyrations like these are often seen at the end of the month and soon normalise.
Dealers said they were still awaiting Bundesbank data which would possibly help rates come off a little bit this afternoon.
Rates are likely to remain firm however this afternoon, slipping back towards the recent rates around three percent.
Bank reserves at the Bundesbank stood at 42.5 billion marks on Wednesday compared with 40.1 while the monthly average would be 39.0 billion marks compared with 38.9 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings on Wednesday stood at 600 million marks compared with 300 million marks a day earlier.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 4.47417 percent on Thursday compared with 3.08592 percent.
